title: Set each tubular latch to its door's backset before fitting it, then drop a spindle through
instruction: Fit a latch in each door edge bore at the length that door needs, then drop a spindle through each.
context: Door hardware fitters use tubular latches whose backset (door edge to the centre of the handle bore) adjusts between two lengths, 60 and 70 mm on real latches. It must be set to the face bore before the latch goes in; set wrong, the hub sits 10 mm off the bore and the spindle will not pass. Done by: locksmiths (O*NET 49-9094.00), carpenters (47-2031.00). Unlike TK-VGVX32 (extend a handle to a marked length) and TK-7F63GM (measure, pick a spacer), the length must be read off each door.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart): 'in front' is away from the arm bases, left and right are the robot's, heights are above the table top. Lot A (the screenshot): two doors (loose but heavy, 3 kg each, white-painted wood slabs, 14 cm front to back, 12 cm wide, 4 cm thick) lie flat on two wooden blocks each (2 x 12 x 2 cm, part of the door), 2 cm above the table, their near edges at 30.0 cm in front, centred 9.0 cm left and 9.0 cm right of the midline. Each has an edge bore, 3.0 cm square, running straight in from the middle of its near edge (centre 4.0 cm high), and a face bore, 1.6 cm square, straight down through the door, centred 7.0 cm in from the edge on the left door and 6.0 cm on the right one. Along both long sides of each door's top runs a row of dark marks, 2 x 12 mm, every 1.0 cm from 1.0 to 13.0 cm in from the near edge. In front of each door a dark-grey bench block, 14 cm long (16.0 to 30.0 cm in front), 6 cm wide and 2.5 cm tall (level with the edge bore's floor), runs up to the door edge and moves with the door. On each bench lies a tubular latch (loose, 75 g) in line with its door's edge bore: a brass faceplate 4 mm thick, 50 mm long (side to side) and 20 mm tall toward the robot, its back at 19.0 cm in front; a steel tube 50 x 16 x 16 mm behind it; and a brass hub (24 mm long, 22 x 22 mm, with a 16 mm square hole straight down through it, a dark 4 x 12 x 4 mm ridge across the top of its back wall) at the tube's far end. The hub slides along the tube and clicks to one of two settings: 60 mm or 70 mm from the faceplate's back to the hub's centre. Both latches start at 60 mm. Two steel spindles, 10 x 10 x 90 mm, 30 g, stand upright in dark holders (3.0 cm square, 3 cm tall, 14 mm square hole) at 24.0 cm in front, 24.0 cm left and right of the midline. Nothing else is on the table. Lot B swaps the two doors, each with its bench block: the 70 mm door is centred 9.0 cm right of the midline and the 60 mm door 9.0 cm left; the latches, spindles and holders stay as in lot A. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end from a photo, a ruler and the video, each door where its lot started it. A latch is fitted in a door when its faceplate's back is at most 3 mm in front of that door's edge and at most 1 mm past it, the latch is within 4 mm of the edge bore's centre line sideways and in height (lying on the bore floor), its tube within 3 degrees of the bore's line, its hub's hole centred within 3 mm of the face bore's centre (so the latch's setting matches that door), and it is at rest. A spindle is through a fitted latch when it stands within 5 degrees of upright, its centre within 8 mm of the face bore's centre, its lower end below the hub's underside, and it is at rest. Released means no part of either gripper within 5 mm of any latch or spindle; at rest means moving less than 1 cm/s. Score 1.0: both doors have a fitted latch with a spindle through it, released. Score 0.5: both doors have a fitted latch, released, but at least one spindle is not through. Score 0 in every other case, including a latch fitted at the wrong setting (its hub 10 mm off the face bore, so a spindle rests on the hub), a faceplate more than 3 mm proud, a latch missing, or anything held. Either latch and either spindle may go in either door. The trial ends at 1.0 once that state has held for 3 s; otherwise it scores the last step. Possible scores per trial: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Push each latch's hub back to the 60 mm setting, stand both latches back on their benches, faceplates toward the robot, and stand both spindles in their holders. Lot A: the door with its face bore 7.0 cm in on the left, the 6.0 cm door on the right, near edges at 30.0 cm in front, centres 9.0 cm either side of the midline. Lot B: lift the two doors (with their blocks and benches) and swap them. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes; no latch bolt, spring bolt or screws. The hub's two settings are a spring slide that clicks to the nearer one past half-way. The bores are square and 3 mm or more larger than the parts. The doors lie flat, so the spindle drops in from above. Release uses the simulator's finger shapes. Two lots swap the doors, which stops one fixed habit but not a memorised replay of both layouts.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
